Title: Chat: Use mouse Back to return to the agent sessions list

Body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

When the Chat view is narrow enough that the agent sessions list is not shown beside the active chat, the mouse Back button should return to the sessions list. This would make mouse navigation consistent with the visible list/detail relationship instead of navigating editor history.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable `workbench.editor.mouseBackForwardToNavigate`.
2. Enable the Chat view's agent sessions list.
3. Open the Chat view and size it so the sessions list and active chat are shown one at a time rather than side by side.
4. Select an existing session from the sessions list.
5. Focus the chat transcript or input.
6. Press the mouse Back button.

## Current behavior

VS Code navigates editor history instead of returning to the agent sessions list.

## Expected behavior

The active chat closes and the agent sessions list is shown and focused. Mouse Back should continue to navigate editor history when the sessions list is already beside the chat, when focus is outside the chat, or when agent sessions are disabled.

Title: Add mute-mic button and transcription controls for ChatGPT voice mode

Body:
Feature request: Add a mute-mic button and transcription controls for ChatGPT voice mode

Background
- ChatGPT voice mode currently does live transcription and supports hands-free input.
- From internal discussion: users would like a dedicated mute/disable-mic button for hands-free use, and reconsideration of whether live transcription should be on by default.

Proposal
- Add a clear, persistent mute/unmute microphone button in ChatGPT voice mode UI so users can temporarily mute their mic without interrupting the voice session.
- Expose a setting to control live transcription default (on/off) and a quick toggle in the voice UI to enable/disable transcription per session.

User benefits
- Prevents accidental audio input during hands-free mode (e.g., background noise, coughing, etc.).
- Gives users control over privacy and reduces interruptions to the model when they need to speak privately.
- Improves accessibility for heavy mute-button users.

Suggested UX details
- Mute button visible next to existing microphone/control area; show visual state (muted/unmuted).
- Muting should stop sending audio to transcription/voice backend but keep the voice session active so users can unmute quickly.
- Provide an optional setting (Preferences → Chat/Voice) to set transcription default (on/off) and to always show the mute button in voice mode.

Title: Add dictation entry point to editor and terminal context menus

Body:
<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Add a dictation entry point to the editor and terminal context menus.

Problem
- Users who rely on speech-to-text/dictation currently have no obvious way to start dictation from the editor or integrated terminal UI.

Proposal
- Add a "Start dictation" (or similarly named) command to the editor context menu and the terminal context menu.
- Do not surface a persistent toolbar button for dictation; keep the entry point confined to context menus and the command palette.

Rationale
- Context menus provide a discoverable, low-clutter way to expose dictation where users are already interacting (editor/terminal) without adding persistent UI that could be distracting.
- This keeps the UI minimal while still making dictation easy to access for users who need it.

Acceptance criteria
- "Start dictation" appears in the editor context menu and the terminal context menu.
- The command is also registerable in the command palette and supports keybinding.
- No new toolbar buttons are added by default.
- Works with the existing accessibility settings and does not regress keyboard/ screen-reader behavior.

Implementation notes
- The command can reuse existing dictation backend (if any) or expose a new command that integrations can hook into.
- Consider telemetry to track usage (opt-in / respecting privacy) and ensure consent for audio input.

References / context
- Internal feedback: add to context menus, but not toolbars.

Title: Keep Omni open after closing the Agents window

Body:
## Feature request

Keep an open Omni bar functional when its owning Agents window is closed.

Today, closing the Agents window also disrupts the Omni bar because the Agents workbench owns services that Omni needs for session routing. Instead, closing the Agents window while Omni is open should hide and retain the owning workbench so Omni remains usable. Closing Omni should then complete the deferred close, while reopening Agents should restore the retained window and cancel that deferred close.

## Expected behavior

- Closing the Agents window does not close or disable an open Omni bar.
- The open Omni bar continues to support session routing.
- Closing Omni finishes closing the hidden Agents window.
- Reopening Agents restores the hidden window and cancels its deferred close.

Implementation: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331312

Title: Agents window: New Session composer snaps back to harness with models on startup

Body:
Summary

When starting a transient VS Code window, signing into GitHub, then opening the Agents window, the New Session composer could switch the selected harness to the first harness with published models (e.g. Codex/Claude) after you explicitly picked another harness (e.g. Copilot). Models arrive asynchronously on startup and that race caused the pick to snap back to the harness that published models first.

Steps to reproduce

1. Launch a transient VS Code instance (not previously signed-in).
2. Sign into GitHub.
3. Open the Agents window and open the New Session composer.
4. Pick a harness that does not yet have a model catalog (for example, Copilot or Codex) while another harness (e.g. Claude) later registers models.
5. Observe that the composer “snaps back” to the harness with models a second or two later.

Expected

The stored harness preference (if any) should win; if no stored preference exists the first harness in the list should be used. Picking a harness in the composer should persist and not be overwritten by asynchronous model-arrival events.

Actual

The composer briefly honored the user pick but then switched to whatever harness had published models first, making the selection feel like it was reverting unexpectedly.

Investigation / Fix
